title: Metal: Refactor; fix dynamic uniforms; acyclic render graph support
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> The majority of the **Files Changed** was to add the metal-cpp headers to `thirdparty/metal-cpp`. This is in the first commit, so that it is easier to see the changes specific to Metal. **146 of the changed files are additions to `thirdparty/metal-cpp`.**

This PR introduces a major refactoring of the Metal rendering driver with three key improvements:

### metal-cpp

Refactors the code to use C++ rather than Objective-C with the following intended benefits:

- make it more approachable for existing rendering developers
- can use existing Godot containers for Metal objects, which are now C++ structs / classes
- consistent with other RDDs, which are pure C++
- Explicit reference counting, to remove ugly `__unsafe_unretained` and other compiler directives to disable ARC
    - This will provide other advantages, including using [command buffers with unretained references](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlcommandqueue/makecommandbufferwithunretainedreferences()?language=objc) to further reduce CPU overhead. We can do this, because we'll be explicitly tracking resources in the Metal RDD.
- Given explicit memory management (no ARC in C++ code), there are cases where generated code could be quite a bit smaller. See [this gist](https://gist.github.com/stuartcarnie/4af9775529dd091cf5213370b38876b6)

### Architecture Refactoring

The primary purpose of these changes were to separate common code that can be shared with Metal 3 and Metal 4. I have a complete Metal 4 renderer working with this branch to prove the refactoring is complete.

- **Split Metal objects**: Renamed `metal_objects.h/mm` → `metal3_objects.h/mm` and extracted shared code into new `metal_objects_shared.h/cpp`
- **New MTL3 namespace**: Created dedicated namespace for Metal 3-specific functionality with `MTL3::RenderingDeviceDriverMetal` class
- **Command buffer hierarchy**: `MDCommandBuffer` now inherits from `MDCommandBufferBase` with virtual methods for polymorphic dispatch to Metal 3 and Metal 4 in the future.
- **Cleaner separation**: Shared types (`MDRenderPass`, `MDAttachment`, `MDSubpass`, `MDFrameBuffer`, shaders, pipelines) moved to shared header for reuse
- **Methods refactored**: `bind_uniforms_argument_buffers` moved from `MDUniformSet` to `MDCommandBuffer`, which is Metal 3 specific

### Dynamic Uniforms Fix

A hack was implemented to disable argument buffers (and use slot binding) when a shader used dynamic uniforms. This has been resolved with this update.

- **Ring buffer allocation**: Added `MDRingBuffer` class for efficient transient GPU memory allocations (16-byte aligned, 64KB default segments)
- **GPU address-based binding**: Dynamic uniform buffers now use `MTLGPUAddress` for argument buffer updates instead of per-frame buffer copies using slot binding, which was a hack.


### Acyclic Render Graph Support

Moving to ARG should provide an overall performance gain, especially when there are a large number of resources (textures and buffers) in use. Overall CPU usage is expected to be lower when ARG is used.

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> ARG is opt-in. Specify `GODOT_MTL_FORCE_BARRIERS=1` to enable the ARG. Eventually it will be available as a project setting.


### Additional Changes

- **MetalFX updates**: Fixes a TODO to handle resource lifetime of scaler objects generically to allow for Metal 4 support in the future.
